text:
morgan: Heads-up — new customer onboarding failing. SSO login returns 500, and SCIM provisioning calls get 400/invalid_payload. Started after the RBAC changes we pushed this morning. Anyone seen this pattern?

dev-bot: Deploy finished 2026-03-21T09:04:02Z for infra/rbac-service @morgan

sara: Can you paste the exact SCIM error payload and any SAML logs? 400 can be a schema mismatch or a required attribute missing.

morgan: Pasting sanitized SCIM request + response:

```
POST /scim/v2/Users
{
  "userName": "jane.doe@example.com",
  "name": {"givenName":"Jane","familyName":"Doe"},
  "externalId": "acct-1234"
}
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],
  "detail": "attribute 'roles' is required for provisioning to this tenant",
  "status": "400"
}
```

morgan: SAML error from auth-proxy: `failed to decrypt assertion: kms:Decrypt failed: access denied`

raj: KMS denial + missing roles in the SCIM response. Sounds like two linked issues: RBAC change removed a role mapping that the SCIM logic expects, and the assertion decryption failing indicates the KMS key permissions might not include the new service account.

elaine: Did we rotate KMS keys or change key policy this morning? ops-bot did a maintenance window around 08:50.

ops-bot: KMS key alias `alias/redwood-sso` rotated at 2026-03-21T08:47:31Z. Rotation triggered by scheduled rekey job. No failures reported at the time.

sara: Ok, two parallel threads to check: 1) RBAC role mapping -> SCIM payload requires `roles` attribute. 2) KMS key policy -> auth-proxy can't decrypt assertions. If the proxy lost kms:Decrypt permission, SAML assertions will fail early.

morgan: Quick check in logs shows auth-proxy attempted decrypt with key-id `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111:key/abcd1234` but KMS returns `AccessDeniedException`. The key policy currently lists principals: `svc-auth-proxy@redwood` and `svc-kms-rotator@redwood`. The new RBAC service account is `svc-rbac@redwood` — not in the policy.

raj: That explains decrypt. But why would SCIM require `roles` now? We changed the default role mapping so tenants with explicit role assignments fallback to `roles` field in SCIM payload. Looks like the onboarding flow expects that field for this customer (they enable role sync). The RBAC change accidentally made role-sync opt-in only.

elaine: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) Add `svc-rbac@redwood` to KMS key policy (temp fix), 2) Patch RBAC service to restore default role mapping, 3) Re-run provisioning for affected tenant with `X-Replay: true` header to replay SCIM events.

morgan: I can push key policy change (low risk, timeboxed) and restart auth-proxy. Who can revert the RBAC mapping change?

raj: I will revert the mapping commit and cut a canary patch to prod route. ETA 20m.

sara: morgan — after you update key policy, post the exact IAM statement you applied. Need it for audit trail. Also open an internal task to validate KMS principal membership against service accounts when rotating keys.

morgan: Applied temporary key policy — added `arn:aws:iam::111111:role/svc-rbac` with decrypt permission. Patch and restart auth-proxy now.

dev-bot: auth-proxy restart triggered by morgan at 2026-03-21T09:18:01Z.

morgan: SAML log after restart: `assertion decrypted, validated audience 'https://redwood.example.com/sso/callback'` — login flow now progresses past SAML.

raj: RBAC mapping revert deployed to canary, monitoring for 5m.

elaine: Replayed SCIM provisioning for tenant `tenant-42` with `X-Replay: true`. First attempt: 200 ok, user created but missing role assignment in app. Checking downstream mapping.

sara: For audit, record these items: key rotation at 08:47, RBAC change deploy at 09:04, auth-proxy failures 09:06–09:18, mitigation timeline. We should file a postmortem with impact: new-customer onboarding delayed ~35m.

morgan: Quick note: Found an edge-case in the SCIM adapter — if `roles` is absent but `groups` present, we attempt a lookup in RBAC service. The revert fixes it, but we should add defensive fallback to avoid throwing 400. Filed PR #4123 to accept empty `roles` and queue a retry if RBAC lookup fails.

elaine: Nice. Also add a test that simulates KMS principal omission during key rotation so we catch this in CI.

raj: Agreed. I'll own the RBAC revert postmortem section. morgan — can you draft the sequence of commands you ran for the key policy change so we can add to the incident timeline?

morgan: Copying commands to incident doc:

```bash
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id abcd1234 --policy-name default > policy.json
# edit policy.json to include role ARN arn:aws:iam::111111:role/svc-rbac
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id abcd1234 --policy-name default --policy file://policy.json
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -n sso
```

morgan: Will open the postmortem and assign follow-ups: add CI test for KMS rotations, RBAC adapter defensive fallback, and run a one-off audit to find other KMS keys missing svc-rbac principal.

sara: Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated, but keeping thread open for PM notes and review. :white_check_mark:
